title: Words carried to hearts
summary: Nephi reflects on the limits of his writing and says some people harden their hearts against the Holy Spirit and cast written things away.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he cannot write all that was taught among his people and is not as mighty in writing as in speaking.
He says words spoken by the power of the Holy Ghost are carried unto people's hearts.
Some harden their hearts against the Holy Spirit and cast many written things away as worthless.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown as the authorial speaker; writing materials are a reasonable visual choice.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, surroundings, writing tools, and any listeners are not specified.

narration.text: I, Nephi, cannot write all the things

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Holy Ghost carrying words to hearts is teaching, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Holy Ghost as a visible figure or invent named people rejecting writings.

title: Prayer for his people
summary: Nephi describes the worth of his writing, his prayers and tears for his people, and his confidence that the Lord will make his words strong for their benefit.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi esteems his writing as valuable, especially to his people.
He prays continually for them by day, his eyes water his pillow by night, and he cries to God in faith, knowing God will hear.
He says the Lord God will consecrate his prayers for his people's gain and his written words will be made strong unto them.
His words persuade people to do good, make their fathers known, speak of Jesus, and persuade belief in him and endurance to the end.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi praying at night beside a pillow is supported by the verse.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, Nephi's appearance, and the form of his writing are not stated.

narration.text: mine eyes water my pillow by night
I know that he will hear my cry.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's consecration and the strengthening of words are statements of belief, not visible events described here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine appearance or specific future readers.

title: Plainness and charity
summary: Nephi describes the plainness of his writing, his glory in truth and Jesus, his charity for his people, the Jews, and the Gentiles, and the need to be reconciled to Christ and continue in the path to life.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says his writing speaks harshly against sin according to the plainness of truth.
He glories in plainness, truth, and Jesus, and says Jesus redeemed his soul from hell.
He has charity for his people and faith in Christ that he will meet many souls spotless at Christ's judgment-seat.
Nephi says he has charity for the Jew and for the Gentiles.
He says they must be reconciled unto Christ, enter the narrow gate, walk the strait path to life, and continue until the end of probation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown alone as the authorial speaker.
unspecified_visual_details: No literal gate, path, judgment-seat, hell, or redemption scene is described.

narration.text: I glory in plainness; I glory in truth
I have charity for my people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The gate, path, judgment-seat, and redemption are teachings or expectations, not narrated present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ, the Jews, the Gentiles, or a literal judgment or gate scene as present.

title: Believe in Christ
summary: Nephi urges his hearers to believe in Christ and his words, speaks of a future judgment, and prays that many may be saved in God's kingdom.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi calls his brethren, the Jew, and all the ends of the earth to hearken and believe in Christ and his words.
He says the words teach all men to do good and that Christ will show at the last day that they are his words.
Nephi says he and his hearers shall stand face to face before Christ's bar and know he was commanded to write.
Nephi prays the Father in Christ's name that many, if not all, may be saved in his kingdom at the great and last day.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown speaking, with his audience off-screen.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience and any judgment scene are not described as visibly present.

narration.text: hearken unto these words and believe in Christ
I pray the Father in the name of Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The judgment and Christ's future showing are future statements, not present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ, a judgment bar, or a gathered audience.

title: Farewell and obedience
summary: Nephi addresses the house of Israel and all the ends of the earth as a voice crying from the dust, bids farewell, warns that his words will condemn those who reject them, and says he must obey the Lord's command.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi speaks to the house of Israel and all the ends of the earth as the voice of one crying from the dust, and bids farewell until the great day.
He bids an everlasting farewell to those who will not partake of God's goodness or respect the words, saying the words will condemn them at the last day.
Nephi says what he seals on earth shall be brought against them at the judgment bar, that the Lord commanded him, and that he must obey.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown as the authorial speaker; the phrase “voice ... from the dust” need not be visualized literally.
unspecified_visual_details: No grave, burial, audience, or present judgment scene is described.

narration.text: I speak unto you as the voice of one crying from the dust

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The voice from the dust and judgment language do not narrate a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Nephi emerging from a grave or Christ at the judgment bar.
